panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: This is a pediatric echocardiogram (echo) showing turbulent flow in the descending aorta in a suprasternal view, which is consistent with Coarctation of the Aorta (CoA), a key component of Shone Complex. B: This Doppler ultrasound image shows specific hemodynamic findings (peak velocity 4 m/s, diastolic flow pattern) across a stenosis in the aorta, strongly indicative of aortic coarctation in the context of Shone Complex.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: The panel shows a parasternal long axis echocardiogram illustrating restricted movement and abnormal morphology of the mitral valve leaflet, consistent with a parachuted mitral valve, a hallmark of Shone Complex. B: The panel shows an apical four-chamber view with color flow Doppler visualizing a mitral regurgitation jet, which is a known clinical consequence of severe valve pathology often associated with Shone Complex.

in_text_mentions: Focused point-of-care echocardiography was performed, which showed poor left ventricular contractility with an ejection fraction visually estimated to be less than 15%, restricted motion of the mitral valve leaflets with abnormal valve morphology, and a mitral regurgitation jet (Image 2 and Video). These findings raised the concern for cardiogenic shock secondary to a previously undiagnosed congenital heart defect. An epinephrine infusion was started to provide inotropic support with improvement in the patient’s blood pressure.

ulations. The “parachute” shape of the mitral valve has a distinct sonographic appearance and may markedly restrict the movement of the valve leaflets, which is easily appreciated on dynamic imaging (Image 2 and Video). Mitral insufficiency and regurgitation can be visualized with color Doppler in the apical four-chamber view. The diagnosis of subaortic stenosis is more complicated requiring measurement of post-stenotic flow velocities.
